svg.title: A merge request that only changes deployment files does not wait for the test suite: Default branch release waits for plan even when plan fails
svg.text: A merge request that only changes deployment files does
not wait for the test suite
Scenario: Default branch release waits for plan even when plan fails

g.text: Given a default branch pipeline with independent plan and release runners
These real GitLab jobs preserve the shipped scheduling rules. A controlled barrier replaces plan's work; a fixture
release writes a version marker. Two separate runners prevent an accidental queue from proving the wait.
Then release advances the branch only after plan succeeds
The branch stays at the pipeline commit until plan finishes; the version marker then advances it. Retrying an obsolete
Then release also runs after plan fails without hiding that failure
Plan remains failed. Release still starts after it finishes, preserving when: always.
Then web and scheduled pipelines wait too and concurrent plans are serialized
The real web pipeline mutation and both existing schedule flags retain the wait. A second plan waits for its resource
group, then its obsolete commit cannot synchronize.
Then release keeps its behavior for merge requests without plan and staging tags
An image-only MR has release without plan. A staging tag still excludes release.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 5 steps · 5 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
